lead.title: Badenoch accused of U-turn after she pledges to bring back tourism VAT refund scheme she scrapped – UK politics live
lead.summary: Tory scrapped the scheme which allowed overseas visitors tax-free shopping when she was a Treasury minister Peter Walker is a senior Guardian political correspondent at the Lib Dem conference in Brighton. It is a brave person who tells John Curtice , the eminent political scientist and guru of British polling, that he doesn’t really understand modern politics, but that’s what Lisa Smart of the Liberal Democrats did at the party’s conference in Brighton. How will the party get back to the 24% it won in 2010? I might gently suggest, Prof Curtice, that with winning 57 seats on 24% in 2010 and winning a record-breaking 72 seats on 12.2% of the vote in 2024, I know which one I prefer. I think John is asking the wrong question. We are not in two-party politics any more. The decision to scrap the VAT refund scheme for international visitors in 2021 left the UK “less competitive” than many other European destinations as the country left the EU, the Tories said. Badenoch, who personally announced the abolition of the VAT refund scheme when she was a Treasury minister in 2020 , said retailers were being “let down by a policy that is driving their customers away.” The Tories have pulled off a spectacular U-turn. Kemi Badenoch used to say tax-free shopping was a costly giveaway and now she’s trying to sell it as an economic miracle. If they really think it’s such a great idea, they should explain why they scrapped it in the first place and how they’d pay for bringing it back. The UK is one of the most-visited countries in the world with international tourism driving billions into our economy. We are supporting the continued growth of this industry and the government is working to meet our ambition to welcome 50 million international visitors a year to the UK by 2030. Visitors can still claim VAT relief where the items purchased are shipped directly to their home country as exports. Continue reading...

top.title: Banished to alien lands – Trump’s secret deportation deals | First Thing
top.summary: Thousands of people deported from the US to countries where they have no connections. Plus, European spy chiefs warn of Moscow action against Nato Good morning. After a plane journey in shackles, an Iranian woman found herself in the middle of Africa in a country she did not know existed. She is one of thousands of people deported from the US on the back of shadowy deals made with dozens of countries. At what scale are third-country deportations happening? Since returning to office in 2025, Donald Trump’s administration has deported more than 25,000 people to countries that are not their own. Which countries are people being deported to? The Trump administration has struck 35 deals allowing it to deport migrants and asylum seekers to countries where they often have no connections. Is this legal? A US federal appeals court ruled on Friday that the Trump administration’s third-country removals policy was unlawful. A three-judge panel unanimously agreed that it violated due process. But the government has 90 days to appeal against the court’s decision, and is expected to do so. How imminent is the threat? “Normunds Mežviets, the director general of the VDD, Latvia’s state security service conceded there were signs that Moscow was making preparations for more decisive action in Europe, but said it was not clear whether the plans were simply part of a destabilisation strategy. “It’s still an open question if they have direct and concrete plans or if it’s just within the context of their overall attempts to spread fear and uncertainty in western society,” he said. European Parliament members have also deplored the vote held in “the world’s least-free territories” which they said were staged under martial law, “amid coercion, forced passportisation, door-to-door balloting in the presence of armed personnel and credible reports of grave human rights violations.” More widely, the Duma vote had been held in the “most repressive environment” with “criminalisation and elimination of political opposition”, read a joint statement from senior Russia and Ukraine EP committee heads. After 62 days of measurements with a highly shielded germanium detector, they found no such signal.
